fields.meta_description: Create a walk-through form tenants and buyers fill in on a phone, with a rating and photo for every room and a signature at the end. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Walk-Through Form That Records Every Room in Photos
fields.hero_description: Build a walk-through form that rates each room, takes photos in place, and saves the signed record to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Every Room on Record, in One Walk
fields.features_subheading: A walk-through form records a property's condition one room at a time. Emergent builds each room's page and the final signature.
fields.feature_1:
The same three ratings in every room

Each room is rated Good, Fair, or Damaged and gets a short note. The room list comes from the unit itself: a studio walk covers 4 rooms and a three-bedroom house covers 11.
fields.feature_2:
Photos taken from inside the form

A Fair or Damaged rating opens the camera before the walker can move on. Every photo is saved to that room with the time it was taken, instead of sitting in a camera roll.
fields.feature_3:
A signature that closes the walk

The final screen lists every rating and asks the tenant to sign. The app captures the signature and keeps it, with the date, on the same record the manager opens later.
fields.feature_4:
Move-out answers beside move-in ones

At move-out the form opens on the record from move-in. Each room shows its earlier rating and photo next to today's, and a room whose rating dropped is marked for review.
fields.feature_5:
Open items go to someone by name

A repair left open goes to one named person by email or in a Slack direct message. You choose who it is and how many days an item may sit before that message goes out.
fields.feature_6:
Code export on paid plans

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building on it. Host the walk-through app anywhere, or fold it into a property system you already run.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Walk-Through Forms Get Filled In
fields.tab_content_1:
Before any boxes arrive, unit 6D is on record

Lionel Rauh gets the keys to unit 6D at Junebrook Flats and walks it with the form open on his phone. He rates 8 rooms and photographs a cracked bathroom tile and a scuffed hallway wall. Then he signs on the last screen. Manager Esmeralda Pike has the signed form by email before the first box comes in.
fields.tab_content_2:
Nine rooms compared, one with a new burn mark

Nine rooms at Thornquist Rentals get walked again when a tenant leaves unit 12. Aurelio Quintanar sees each room's move-in photo next to the one he takes today. Eight rooms match. The kitchen counter now has a burn mark. The kitchen goes on his review list with both photos attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of the four agreed repairs, one still fails

The inspection on 19 Ardmore Terrace ended with four agreed repairs. The buyers walk the house the day before closing and mark each one on a phone. Three are done. The garage door still will not close. That line goes to buyer's agent Wynona Castellanos by email, with the buyers' photo of the door.
fields.tab_content_4:
Eleven items by trade, with the oldest sent to Gideon

Eleven items came out of the Lot 27 walk-through at Halcyon Ridge Homes: 5 paint, 3 drywall, 2 trim, and 1 plumbing. Each one sits on a board under its trade. The plumbing item, a dripping hose bib, has been open 9 days. Any item open past 7 days goes to superintendent Gideon Varga in a Slack direct message.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Walk-Through Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a walk-through form with a photo rule and a named person for every open item.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the rooms per unit type
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the rooms in each unit type you walk, down to the laundry closet and the patio. A one-bedroom apartment might have 6 rooms and a new single-family house 14. The form builds one page per room from that list.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each room the same three ratings: Good, Fair, or Damaged. A short note field sits under each one. Keep the scale identical at move-in and move-out, because the comparison only works when both walks use the same words.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a photo whenever a room is rated Fair or Damaged, and leave it optional for Good. Tell walkers to shoot the whole wall first and the damage up close second. That way the reviewer can place it in the room.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who signs at the end of the walk: the tenant alone, or the tenant and the manager together. The last screen lists every rating before anyone signs. Then pick the person who receives the signed copy by email.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the room list and the photo rule into one prompt, and name the signer. Emergent builds the walk-through form and the database behind it, plus a screen of past walks for each unit. Ask in plain English when a room needs adding later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Point open items at a person
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name the person who hears about anything left open, plus a backup for when that person is away. Damaged rooms might go to maintenance and failed repairs to the agent. Agree on a deadline for each kind of item before the first walk.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Walk a vacant unit yourself before the first tenant does. Rate one room Damaged, take the photo, and sign. Then check that the email reaches the manager and the record lands in the table under the right unit.

faq_plan.a: A walk-through form is a room-by-room record of a property's condition, filled in while someone walks through it. Each room gets a rating and a short note, plus a photo of anything worn or broken. You might fill one in at move-in, at move-out, before a home sale closes, or when a builder hands over a new house.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a walk-through form?
faq_plan.a: List the rooms, pick one rating scale, and decide when a photo is required and who signs. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds a form people complete on their phones, with every walk saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How is a final walk-through form different from a move-in one?
faq_plan.hint: Is a final walk through form mandatory?
faq_plan.a: It checks a sale instead of a tenancy. A final walk-through form lists the repairs agreed after the inspection and marks each one done or not done, with a photo. A move-in form rates every room for condition. Build the final version around the repair list, and leave the room ratings out.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with repairs found on a walk-through form?
faq_plan.hint: What is the purpose of a walk-through form in school?
faq_plan.a: Log each one as its own repair, with its photo and the person who will fix it. A walk-through record says what is wrong; a service request form puts the fix in a queue with a date. The app Emergent builds can pass each repair to a maintenance tool through its API.

faq_plan.q: Should the tenant and the landlord both sign the walk-through form?
faq_plan.hint: What is title scope in a walk through form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for both signatures when you can. Two signatures show that both sides saw the same ratings and photos on the same day. Walk the unit together, then have each person sign on the last screen, where the app captures both signatures.

faq_plan.q: Can I fill out a walk-through form on a phone instead of paper?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A phone keeps each photo with the room it belongs to, which a printed walk through form pdf cannot do. The tenant rates rooms and signs on the same screen where the pictures are taken. A form built with Emergent has no response caps, however many units you walk each month.

faq_plan.q: Where should a signed walk-through form be kept?
faq_plan.a: Keep it with the lease for the same unit. Save the signed walk-through next to the rental agreement form, and both open together when the tenant leaves. Built with Emergent, both records sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How should a walk-through form compare move-out photos with move-in ones?
faq_plan.a: Side by side, one room at a time. Take each move-out photo from the spot where the move-in photo was taken, framing the same wall. A reviewer then opens only the rooms whose rating dropped, instead of every photo in the unit.

faq_plan.q: Do walk-through forms work for new construction?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a different list. On a new home, walk through forms log each unfinished item with its trade, such as paint, drywall, or plumbing, instead of rating rooms. Sort open items by trade and by days open. Then each crew sees its own list.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a new walk-through form when a tenant sublets?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Walk the unit on the subtenant's first day, even if the original tenant did one at the start of the lease. Attach that record to the sublease form. It then shows what the unit looked like before the subtenant moved in.
